name: WISE J085510.83-071442.5
summary: Coldest known brown dwarf (≈250 K), ~7.3 ly away, with high proper motion (≈8.1″/yr).
whatIsIt: WISE 0855-0714 is a planetary-mass sub-brown dwarf (mass 3–10 M_Jup) with an atmospheric temperature near freezing (≈250 K), hosting water ice cloud decks.
whyDoesItMove: It is only ≈7.3 light-years away. Its moderate space motion of ≈52 km/s translates into an apparent angular shift of ≈8.1″/yr on the sky.
planetXContext: Like a hypothetical Planet X, WISE 0855 is cold, virtually invisible in optical surveys, and shines primarily in the 4.5–5.0 µm thermal infrared window where SPHEREx operates.

name: Barnard's Star (Gl 699)
summary: Highest known proper motion star (≈10.3″/yr), second-closest stellar system to the Sun.
whatIsIt: An M-dwarf star in Ophiuchus with the largest known proper motion of any star relative to the Solar System.
whyDoesItMove: At 5.96 light-years away, its high transverse velocity (≈90 km/s) produces a massive northward displacement across background stars.
planetXContext: High-proper-motion stars are standard astrometric testbeds to verify that difference imaging cleanly cancels stationary stars while leaving a clear dipole on the mover.

name: Epsilon Indi Ba,Bb
summary: Nearby binary T-dwarf system (T1 + T6) with prominent methane and water vapor absorption.
whatIsIt: A binary system of two cool brown dwarfs (≈47 and ≈28 Jupiter masses) orbiting each other with a period of ≈15 years.
whyDoesItMove: At 11.8 light-years, it shares the fast galactic space motion of the parent star Epsilon Indi A, shifting ≈4.7″/yr.
planetXContext: Its near-infrared spectrum shows the deep molecular absorption windows that SPHEREx spectrophotometry uses to separate substellar bodies from background stars.

name: 136472 Makemake
summary: Distant dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt (≈52 AU), illustrating slow outer Solar System motion.

pmTotal.source: Dominantly annual reflex parallax at 52 AU

whatIsIt: A large Kuiper Belt dwarf planet (diameter ≈1,430 km) covered in frozen methane and ethane.
whyDoesItMove: Its slow orbital speed (≈4.4 km/s) at 52 AU means apparent movement is dominated by Earth's annual parallax reflex.
planetXContext: Demonstrates what real distant Solar System bodies look like in multi-epoch difference images: a small annual loop rather than a fast linear trajectory.

name: R Draconis
summary: Pulsating red giant with large brightness swings (≈245-day cycle); position remains stationary.
whatIsIt: A pulsating red giant (Asymptotic Giant Branch) star expanding and cooling rhythmically with a period of ≈245.6 days.
whyDoesItMove: It does NOT move perceptibly (proper motion < 0.01″/yr at 2,100 ly). Its physical position stays fixed on the sky.
planetXContext: Crucial distinction: In difference imaging, variable stars create a monopole (single spot changing intensity), whereas moving objects create a distinctive dipole (bright spot paired with dark spot).

name: Planet X Search Field (Batygin & Brown 2021)
summary: Representative outer Solar System field (~450 AU) modeled from extreme TNO orbital clustering.

distance.source: Batygin et al. (2019, 2021) model range 380–550 AU

whatIsIt: A predicted 5–10 Earth-mass planet proposed to explain the orbital clustering of extreme trans-Neptunian objects.
whyDoesItMove: At ≈450 AU, orbital motion is only ≈1.4 km/s. Apparent motion is dominated by Earth's annual parallax reflex (≈0.16″/yr).
planetXContext: Because reflected sunlight is faint (scaling as 1/r⁴), SPHEREx detects it via internal thermal emission in Band 6 (4.5–5.0 µm) by differencing all-sky surveys taken 6 months apart.
